target_customer: Independent service professionals such as hairstylists, bartenders and DJs, and the consumers who hire them
problem: Independent professionals struggle to keep their clients when they change venues, and consumers lack a way to follow and discover them.
business_model: free profiles for professionals; revenue model not stated in sources

competitors.name: Thumbtack
competitors.what: Local services marketplace connecting buyers with professionals
competitors.traction_then: 250,000 buyer and seller connections by March 2011 (Vator)

technical_complexity.rationale: Profile pages, galleries, follower updates and cross posting to Twitter and Facebook (TechCrunch, August 2011) are standard web work.

defensibility.rationale: Value depended on professionals bringing followers, which could create a network but was easy to copy early on.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes an incumbent response.

market_need_then: TechCrunch framed it in August 2011 around professionals losing clients when they switch workplaces; no demand metrics were found.

branding.domain_note: Exact .com opez.com per the YC page; no history found.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and personal: the YC description speaks of professionals who 'love what they do' and addresses readers as 'friends'.

brand_strength.rationale: Invented name with no stated meaning and no sign of press on the brand or community; the tagline 'Yelp for service pros' did the explaining.

outcome_analysis: Opez pitched a social profile network for independent service professionals and had 11 people listed by YC, but no funding amounts, traction numbers, exit or shutdown account was found. The cause of its inactive status is not public, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: opez.com returned HTTP 503 so the site is treated as unavailable. One aggregator (altss) lists family office investors without an amount or date; that is unverified and not recorded as a round. TechCrunch calls it Yelp meets Facebook; the YC page says New York and San Francisco. Thumbtack source is a 2011 piece; the traction figure comes from a Vator article of unknown date and is approximate.
